title: How to choose a developer tool without starting with hype
summary: A repeatable selection method with an explicit stopping rule.

sections.heading: Write a decision brief
paragraphs: Describe the task, current workflow and three non-negotiable constraints. For example: maintain an existing TypeScript application, retain repository ownership and stay inside an approved monthly budget. Keep preferences separate from requirements.

sections.heading: Collect comparable evidence
paragraphs: Use official documentation for supported capabilities and current billing terms. Record the date and exact plan. Treat missing facts as questions, not negative answers. Separate a vendor claim from a result you have reproduced.

sections.heading: Trial the smallest reversible change
paragraphs: Use a branch and synthetic data. Set a failing acceptance test, review the proposed diff, run the tests and rehearse rollback. Do not grant production access merely to shorten a demo.

sections.heading: Choose and revisit
paragraphs: Write why you chose the tool, which evidence could change the decision and when to review it. A decision record is more reusable than a universal score. Cancel or reduce the trial if the key constraint remains unresolved.

verdict: Define the acceptance test before selecting the vendor.
bestFor: Developers writing a repeatable evaluation and an exit plan
notFor: Readers looking for unmeasured speed or accuracy rankings
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
